findings.desc: Docs describe dispatch_auto as starting only after host unattended-safety checks pass, but the reusable probe fact never becomes true for Claude and the scheduler bypasses it with a Claude-specific subset check. This keeps v1.0.1 behavior conservative enough, but leaves the host-neutral safety boundary under-specified for future hosts/extensions.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by clarifying README.md and docs/requirements/decisions/host-overflow.md: standalone host_runtime_probe.unattendedSafe remains conservative false; dispatch_auto performs composed authorization using policy, Claude availability, --print support, command allowlist, timeout, env, and scope gates.

findings.desc: CHK-002:edge:0 overclaims explicit opt-in coverage. The intent requires that a claude-code policy without allowRealHostSubprocess=true stays supervised/refused for real subprocess launch, but the recorded evidence points to dispatch-run-smoke paths that only cover host-not-in-policy and gemini unavailable/unattendedSafe=false refusals, not the dedicated claude-code missing-opt-in branch. The production code has a separate refusal at lattice-dispatch.ts:2747-2750, yet unattended-dispatch-smoke only exercises allowRealHostSubprocess=true success/env/nonzero/timeout cases.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by adding unattended-dispatch-smoke coverage for claude-code policy missing allowRealHostSubprocess=true with fake claude on PATH; dispatch_auto refuses before creating dispatch records.

findings.desc: CHK-005:adversarial:0 records a manual_transcript canary, but the story has no persisted transcript artifact or delivery-check style record for that CLI entrypoint run. The checklist note claims a temp git repo canary via node packages/main/dist/cli.js reached runnerKind=claude-code-real, yet B-8a1a contains no evidence/transcript-diff.md, summary.json, or delivery-check.json, so the claimed CLI canary is not independently auditable and currently rests on checklist prose only.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by adding .koala/story/actives/B-8a1a/evidence/cli-real-claude-canary.md with auditable CLI fake-Claude command sequence and JSON result summary; checklist evidence now references the artifact.

findings.desc: [HIGH] packages/main/src/core/lattice-dispatch.ts:1114-1116 uses pathResolvesWithinRoot() without rejecting absolute relative() results. On Windows, cross-drive paths make path.relative() return an absolute path (for example D:\outside), so the current check can treat a symlinked ancestor or registered worktree outside the repo as in-root. That weakens the worktree/path safety boundary for dispatch scopes. Fix by mirroring the stricter handler check and rejecting isAbsolute(rel) before accepting the path as contained.

[HIGH] packages/main/src/core/lattice-dispatch.ts:2626-2638 and 1833-1839 only apply commandAllowlist to pack.requiredCommands; the actual claude child_process launch is unconditional once allowRealHostSubprocess=true. A policy can authorize real Claude subprocess execution even when commandAllowlist does not contain claude --print, which breaks the promised child_process boundary. Fix by validating the real-host launcher against a canonical allowlist entry (for example claude --print <prompt-file>) before dispatch_auto/runDispatch can spawn it.
